strings.d1.s0.name: Fira Caldera Walking Path
strings.d1.s0.tips: Fira's caldera edge: white cubes, blue domes and the volcano across the water.
strings.d1.s1.name: Museum of Prehistoric Thera
strings.d1.s1.tips: Akrotiri frescoes (the Blue Monkeys). Small but essential.
strings.d1.s2.name: Fira Catholic Cathedral & Streets
strings.d1.s2.tips: White and yellow cathedral, Gold Street shops, and donkeys (don't ride them).
strings.d1.s3.name: Argo Restaurant Fira
strings.d1.s3.tips: Caldera views, with fish and fava (yellow split pea purée).
strings.d1.s4.name: Fira Sunset Cable Car & Old Port
strings.d1.s4.tips: Take the cable car (6 EUR) down to the old port for the lights of the ships. Return by cable car or climb the 588 steps.
strings.d1.b0.name: Lucky's Souvlakis Fira
strings.d1.b0.tips: Cheap gyros, instead of caldera prices.
strings.d1.b1.name: Santozeum / Megaro Gyzi
strings.d1.b1.tips: Photos of the 1956 earthquake in the Gyzi Mansion. A museum alternative.
strings.d2.s0.name: Skaros Rock
strings.d2.s0.tips: One hour from Fira along the caldera path (set off at 07:00 in summer). The Venetian castle rock below Imerovigli has the best view and is free.
strings.d2.s1.name: Imerovigli–Oia Trail
strings.d2.s1.tips: Profitis Ilias chapel and a ridge of volcanic rock, then the descent into Oia. Carry 1.5 litres of water.
strings.d2.s2.name: Melitini Oia
strings.d2.s2.tips: Oia's meze restaurant for lunch, with a sea-view terrace.
strings.d2.s3.name: Ammoudi Bay
strings.d2.s3.tips: A fishing cove 300 steps below Oia. Swim off the rocks and eat at the Ammoudi tavernas.
strings.d2.s4.name: Oia Castle
strings.d2.s4.tips: The ruins of Agios Nikolaos castle and a world-famous sunset. Grab a spot an hour early (or book a restaurant). It's crowded, with a bus back.
strings.d2.b0.name: Sunset Ammoudi Taverna
strings.d2.b0.tips: Grilled octopus down in the bay at Ammoudi.
strings.d2.b1.name: Atlantis Books Oia
strings.d2.b1.tips: A cave-like bookshop, instead of the bay.
strings.d3.s0.name: Nea Kameni Volcano Boat
strings.d3.s0.tips: Boat from the old port (tours 30-50 EUR) to the volcanic island.
strings.d3.s1.name: Nea Kameni Crater Walk
strings.d3.s1.tips: A black lava path climbs 130 m to the crater, with sulphur fumes. Park fee 5 EUR.
strings.d3.s2.name: Palea Kameni Hot Springs
strings.d3.s2.tips: Jump off the boat and swim to the muddy 35°C water (wear a dark swimsuit).
strings.d3.s3.name: Thirassia Island Lunch
strings.d3.s3.tips: A quiet island across the caldera. Eat at a taverna in Korfos village (if included in your tour), with steps up to Manolas.
strings.d3.s4.name: Back to Oia via Ammoudi
strings.d3.s4.tips: The boat returns to Ammoudi or Fira.
strings.d3.b0.name: Catamaran Caldera Tour
strings.d3.b0.tips: A catamaran to Red Beach, White Beach and the hot springs, with food and drinks included. An alternative to the volcano tour (afternoon sunset version).
strings.d3.b1.name: To Psaraki Vlychada
strings.d3.b1.tips: Fish at Vlychada harbour, if you're not on a tour.
strings.d4.s0.name: Akrotiri Archaeological Site
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Minoan Pompeii of 1600 BC, with three-storey houses preserved under ash. Roofed, so go in the morning.
strings.d4.s1.name: Red Beach
strings.d4.s1.tips: A beach below red cliffs, with a rockfall warning. Look from the top and swim briefly.
strings.d4.s2.name: Akrotiri Lighthouse
strings.d4.s2.tips: An 1892 lighthouse at the island's southwestern tip, with views.
strings.d4.s3.name: The Cave of Nikolas Akrotiri
strings.d4.s3.tips: A beach taverna at Akrotiri. Try tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters) and fava.
strings.d4.s4.name: Vlychada Beach
strings.d4.s4.tips: A rocky beach with a moonscape view. Quiet, next to the Tomato Industrial Museum.
strings.d4.b0.name: Tomato Industrial Museum Vlychada
strings.d4.b0.tips: A tomato paste factory from 1945, and the story of Santorini's tiny tomato.
strings.d4.b1.name: Dolphins Akrotiri Beach Taverna
strings.d4.b1.tips: A wooden taverna over the water.
strings.d5.s0.name: Pyrgos Village & Kastelli
strings.d5.s0.tips: The island's highest village, with a Venetian castle quarter and 360° views. Few tourists.
strings.d5.s1.name: Santo Wines Pyrgos
strings.d5.s1.tips: A cooperative with caldera views. Taste Assyrtiko and Vinsanto (6 wines), with meze.
strings.d5.s2.name: Megalochori
strings.d5.s2.tips: A quiet village with a bell tower, wine cellars and a square.
strings.d5.s3.name: Venetsanos Winery
strings.d5.s3.tips: A 1947 winery carved into the cliff. Go early, before sunset.
strings.d5.s4.name: Domaine Sigalas Oia
strings.d5.s4.tips: The island's best Assyrtiko, with tastings and cheese in the vineyard.
strings.d5.b0.name: Art Space Winery Exo Gonia
strings.d5.b0.tips: An art gallery in a cave winery, instead of Venetsanos.
strings.d5.b1.name: Metaxy Mas Exo Gonia
strings.d5.b1.tips: A favourite taverna with locals. Book ahead. An alternative to Santo.
strings.d6.theme: East coast beaches: Perissa and Kamari
strings.d6.s0.name: Ancient Thera
strings.d6.s0.tips: A Dorian-Roman city on Mesa Vouno mountain. A zigzag road from Kamari (taxi or scooter) leads to the agora and the sea.
strings.d6.s1.name: Perissa Black Beach
strings.d6.s1.tips: 7 km of black sand, with sunbeds, shallow water and water sports.
strings.d6.s2.name: Perivolos Tranquilo Beach Bar
strings.d6.s2.tips: A sustainable beach bar serving couscous and burgers.
strings.d6.s3.name: Kamari Beach
strings.d6.s3.tips: Across the mountain from Perissa. A promenade and black pebbles, plus an open-air cinema (summer).
strings.d6.s4.name: Kamari Open Air Cinema
strings.d6.s4.tips: Films and cocktails in a garden (May-October).
strings.d6.b0.name: Monastery Kamari
strings.d6.b0.tips: A restaurant in a monastery courtyard in Kamari.
strings.d6.b1.name: Eleftherios Venizelos Museum Kamari
strings.d6.b1.tips: A small museum, for rainy days instead of the beach.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mezzo Imerovigli
strings.d7.s0.tips: Breakfast with caldera views. Quiet in the morning, with Greek yoghurt and honey.
strings.d7.s1.name: Anastasi Church Imerovigli
strings.d7.s1.tips: A blue dome and bell. Visit after breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Fira Factory Shop
strings.d7.s2.tips: Souvenirs: Vinsanto, capers, fava and volcanic stone, in Fira.
strings.d7.s3.name: Santorini Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: 20 minutes by bus from Fira, or 25 EUR by taxi. Time to say goodbye (30 minutes to Athinios port if leaving by ferry).
strings.d7.b0.name: Mama's House Fira
strings.d7.b0.tips: A legendary cheap, huge breakfast near the Fira bus station.
strings.d7.b1.name: Skaros Morning Walk
strings.d7.b1.tips: Back to the rock, instead of souvenir shopping.
strings.note0: KTEL buses run from Fira (Oia 20 min, Perissa 30 min, 2 EUR). ATVs and scooters cost 25-40 EUR a day, and taxis are scarce (25-40 EUR). Buses serve the airport and Athinios port.
strings.note1: Summer temperatures are 28-33°C with the meltemi wind (strong in July and August). Oia's 20:30 sunset is very crowded (arrive an hour early). Fira is packed on cruise ship days (leave before 14:00). August is the most expensive month.
strings.note2: Akrotiri 12 EUR, Thera 6, volcano tour 30-50, catamaran 120+, wine tasting 20-30. Caldera restaurants cost 30-50, Perissa 15-20. Round up the bill for a tip.
strings.note3: Fava (yellow split pea purée), tomatokeftedes, chlorotyri cheese, white aubergine, Assyrtiko and Vinsanto. Santorini tomatoes are tiny.
strings.note4: Do the caldera hike at 7-8 in the morning (in summer). Don't ride the donkeys. Luggage can't be carried in Oia (steps), so stay in Fira or Imerovigli.
strings.note5: The hot springs stain swimwear, and Red Beach has a rockfall warning.
